outlook.statement: HML is committed to building a future-ready and climate-smart agricultural model combining sustainable business practices with innovation, inclusivity, environmental responsibility, and long-term value creation.
Remaining rubber estates expected to receive EUDR compliance confirmation by December 2026.
Expansion plans underway for drip irrigation in all replanted tea fields following successful pilot at Surianalle estate.

The company is taking continuous steps for improvement in quality of tea and rubber products. Cost control measures have been initiated at gardens and rubber units. These measures should help in better price realization of tea and improvement in efficiency of rubber units. All the company's tea gardens and rubber estates are producing quality teas and Rubber. The yields are improving gradually with stress on quality. This should increase the profit margin substantially.

Tea sector expected to remain resilient in FY 2026-27 with stable domestic consumption and steady export demand; CTC to remain backbone, Orthodox to sustain export revenues, Green tea to expand gradually.

Rubber sector likely to continue upward output trajectory supported by state incentives and expansion in non-traditional areas (Northeast); India will continue to rely on imports to bridge structural demand-supply gap; consumption firm with tyre industry anchoring ~64% demand.

Stabilization in global rubber prices expected; projected volume growth in tea and rubber yields from existing and newly integrated operations positions company for strengthened financial performance.
